backup_plan_id.description: The ID of the backup plan
backup_plan_id.rationale: Plan ID has no impact on the security of the resource or data contained.

backup_vault.description: Backup vault where the backups gets stored using this Backup plan.
backup_vault.rationale: This is a resource reference rather than a generic explicit security control.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

description.description: The description allows for additional details about 'BackupPlan' and its use cases to be provided.
description.rationale: Description has no impact on the security of the resource or data contained.

location.description: The location for the backup plan
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

log_retention_days.description: This is only applicable for CloudSql resource. Days for which logs will be stored. This value should be greater than or equal to minimum enforced log retention duration of the backup vault.
log_retention_days.rationale: Log retention is security-relevant because retained logs support security auditing, monitoring, and incident investigation. A retention period that is too short can reduce visibility and forensic capability.

max_custom_on_demand_retention_days.description: The maximum number of days for which an on-demand backup taken with custom retention can be retained.
max_custom_on_demand_retention_days.rationale: Max custom ondemand retention days is a configuration setting and does not directly impact security.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Project is an administrative scoping field and not a direct explicit security control

resource_type.description:
The resource type to which the 'BackupPlan' will be applied.
Examples include, "compute.googleapis.com/Instance", "compute.googleapis.com/Disk", "sqladmin.googleapis.com/Instance", "alloydb.googleapis.com/Cluster", "file.googleapis.com/Instance" and "storage.googleapis.com/Bucket".
resource_type.rationale: his affects compatibility and intended usage, but it is better handled through service-specific validation rather than a explicit security control

backup_rules.backup_retention_days.description: Configures the duration for which backup data will be kept. The value should be greater than or equal to minimum enforced retention of the backup vault.
backup_rules.backup_retention_days.rationale: Lower period of retention increases data loss and compliance risk.

backup_rules.rule_id.description: The unique ID of this 'BackupRule'. The 'rule_id' is unique per 'BackupPlan'.
backup_rules.rule_id.rationale: This is a identifier only and does not impact security controls for this service.

backup_rules.standard_schedule.description: StandardSchedule defines a schedule that runs within the confines of a defined window of days.

backup_rules.standard_schedule.days_of_m.description: Specifies days of months like 1, 5, or 14 on which jobs will run.
backup_rules.standard_schedule.days_of_m.rationale: This is conditional schedule logic and is better handled through custom validation

backup_rules.standard_schedule.days_of_w.description: Specifies days of week like MONDAY or TUESDAY, on which jobs will run. This is required for 'recurrence_type', 'WEEKLY' and is not applicable otherwise. Possible values: ["DAY_OF_WEEK_UNSPECIFIED", "MONDAY", "TUESDAY", "WEDNESDAY", "THURSDAY", "FRIDAY", "SATURDAY", "SUNDAY"]
backup_rules.standard_schedule.days_of_w.rationale: This is conditional schedule logic and is better handled through custom validation

backup_rules.standard_schedule.hourly_fr.description:
Specifies frequency for hourly backups. An hourly frequency of 2 means jobs will run every 2 hours from start time till end time defined.
This is required for 'recurrence_type', 'HOURLY' and is not applicable otherwise.
backup_rules.standard_schedule.hourly_fr.rationale: This is conditional and depends on recurrence type, so no security impact by itself.

backup_rules.standard_schedule.months.description: Specifies values of months Possible values: ["MONTH_UNSPECIFIED", "JANUARY", "FEBRUARY", "MARCH", "APRIL", "MAY", "JUNE", "JULY", "AUGUST", "SEPTEMBER", "OCTOBER", "NOVEMBER", "DECEMBER"]
backup_rules.standard_schedule.months.rationale: This is conditional schedule logic and is better handled through custom validation

backup_rules.standard_schedule.recurrenc.description: RecurrenceType enumerates the applicable periodicity for the schedule. Possible values: ["HOURLY", "DAILY", "WEEKLY", "MONTHLY", "YEARLY"]
backup_rules.standard_schedule.recurrenc.rationale: Frequency period impacts recovery and compliance. Values outside the approved range increase data loss and compliance risk.

backup_rules.standard_schedule.time_zone.description: The time zone to be used when interpreting the schedule.
backup_rules.standard_schedule.time_zone.rationale: This affects operational timing, but it is not usually enforced as an explicit security control.

backup_rules.standard_schedule.backup_wi.description:
A BackupWindow defines the window of the day during which backup jobs will run. Jobs are queued at the beginning of the window and will be marked as
'NOT_RUN' if they do not start by the end of the window.

The hour of the day (1-24) when the window ends, for example, if the value of end hour of the day is 10, that means the backup window end time is 10:00.
The end hour of the day should be greater than the start
backup_rules.standard_schedule.backup_wi.rationale: This is an operational scheduling field, not an explicit security control

backup_rules.standard_schedule.backup_wi.description: The hour of the day (0-23) when the window starts, for example, if the value of the start hour of the day is 6, that means the backup window starts at 6:00.
backup_rules.standard_schedule.backup_wi.rationale: This is an operational scheduling field, not an explicit security control

backup_rules.standard_schedule.week_day_.description: Specifies a week day of the month like FIRST SUNDAY or LAST MONDAY, on which jobs will run.
Specifies the day of the week. Possible values: ["DAY_OF_WEEK_UNSPECIFIED", "MONDAY", "TUESDAY", "WEDNESDAY", "THURSDAY", "FRIDAY", "SATURDAY", "SUNDAY"]
WeekOfMonth enumerates possible weeks in the month, e.g. the first, third, or last week of the month. Possible values: ["WEEK_OF_MONTH_UNSPECIFIED", "FIRST", "SECOND", "THIRD", "FOURTH", "LAST"]

compute_instance_backup_plan_properties.description: Defines optional compute instance related properties for backups generated by this plan.

compute_instance_backup_plan_properties..description:
Indicates whether to perform a guest flush operation before taking a
compute instance backup. When set to true, the system will attempt
to ensure application-consistent backups.

disk_backup_plan_properties.description: Defines optional disk related properties for backups generated by this plan.

disk_backup_plan_properties.guest_flush.description:
Indicates whether to perform a guest flush operation before taking a disk
backup. When set to true, the system will attempt to ensure
application-consistent backups. When set to false, the system will
create crash-consistent backups.
